tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a message from the system confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a message from the system confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

schema.name: Workflow
schema.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a message from the system confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a message from the system confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

The cache is positional: agent() calls replay from cache up to the first call that failed, no longer matches the earlier run (edited, added, removed or reordered) or never started in it; that call and every call after it run again, even when their own (prompt, opts) are unchanged. A call a usage limit refused, or one still running when the run stopped, usually runs again without ending reuse: finished calls after it still come from cache. Same-session only. 358	        self.state_dict_load_opts = state_dict_load_opts or dist_cp_sd.StateDictOptions(
359	            flatten_optimizer_state_dict=True, strict=True
360	        )
361	        self.load_key_mapping = load_key_mapping
362	        self.reset_optimizer_states_on_load = reset_optimizer_states_on_load
363	        self.reset_optimizer_states_on_resume = reset_optimizer_states_on_resume
364	
365	        self.optim = None
366	        if not self.eval_only:
367	            # Build optimizer(s).
368	            log.info("Building optimizer...")
369	
370	            from olmo_core.optim.moe_optimizer import OLMoDDPOptimizerConfig
371	
372	            assert isinstance(optim, OLMoDDPOptimizerConfig)
373	            optim = cast(OLMoDDPOptimizerConfig, optim)
374	            self.optim = optim.build(
375	                self.model_parts,
376	                self,
377	                strict=False,  # group_overrides might only be matched in one group, strict=False allows it to not match in one group (could match in some other group),
378	            )
379	
380	            # MultiGroupDDP owns normal-parameter reduction. Keep the optimizer's
381	            # older post-backward reducer disabled so FP8WeightStore gradients stay
382	            # on their existing, independent synchronization path.
383	            if self.use_reduce_scatter:
384	                sharded_params = self.optim.normal_params_with_sharded_optimizer_state()
385	                unconfigured_params = set(sharded_params)
386	                for model_part in self.model_parts:
387	                    if not isinstance(model_part, MultiGroupDistributedDataParallel):
388	                        raise RuntimeError(
389	                            "use_reduce_scatter=True requires MultiGroupDistributedDataParallel."
390	                        )
391	                    local_sharded_params = sharded_params.intersection(
392	                        model_part.param_to_process_group
393	                    )
394	                    model_part.configure_reduce_scatter_params(local_sharded_params)
395	                    unconfigured_params.difference_update(local_sharded_params)
396	                if unconfigured_params:
397	                    raise RuntimeError(
398	                        "Some optimizer-sharded normal parameters are not managed by "
399	                        "any MultiGroupDistributedDataParallel model part."
400	                    )
401	        else:
402	            log.info("Skipping optimizer build because eval_only=True")

439	    def _build_world_mesh(
440	        self,
441	        *,
442	        dp: Optional[DataParallelConfig] = None,
443	        tp: Optional[TensorParallelConfig] = None,
444	        cp: Optional[ContextParallelConfig] = None,
445	        pp: Optional[PipelineParallelConfig] = None,
446	        ep: Optional[ExpertParallelConfig] = None,
447	        device_type: Optional[str] = None,
448	    ) -> None:
449	        """
450	        Build a :class:`~torch.distributed.device_mesh.DeviceMesh` suitable for the given parallel strategies.
451	
452	        .. seealso::
453	            Pass the mesh created by this function to any of the ``get_*_mesh()`` functions in
454	            this module to get the right sub-mesh for a any given parallel strategy.
455	
456	            - :func:`get_dp_model_mesh()` gives you the 1 or 2D sub-mesh suitable for data parallel *model*
457	            wrappers like FSDP(2) or DDP.
458	            - :func:`get_dp_mesh()` gives you the 1D sub-mesh suitable for configuring *data loaders*.
459	            - :func:`get_tp_mesh()` gives you the 1D sub-mesh for tensor parallelism.
460	            - :func:`get_cp_mesh()` gives you the 1D sub-mesh for context parallelism.
461	            - :func:`get_pp_mesh()` gives you the 1D sub-mesh for pipeline parallelism.
462	            - :func:`get_ep_mesh()` gives you the 1D sub-mesh for expert parallelism.
463	
464	        .. important::
465	            A data parallel config is required if any other parallel config is set.
466	
467	        .. important::
468	            Not all parallel strategies are compatible with each other.
469	
470	        :param dp: Data parallel config.
471	        :param tp: Tensor parallel config.
472	        :param cp: Context parallel config.
473	        :param pp: Pipeline parallel config.
474	        :param ep: Expert parallel config.
475	        :param device_type: The device type.
476	
477	        :returns: The world mesh with a shape compatible with the given parallel configs.
478	        """
479	
480	        if len(self.world_mesh) > 0:
481	            raise RuntimeError(
482	                "world mesh already exists! You can only call 'build_world_mesh' once!"
483	            )
484	
485	        device_type = device_type or get_default_device().type
486	        dp_world_size = get_world_size()
487	
488	        # no config, Pure DP
489	        # if pp is None and tp is None and cp is None and dp is None and ep is None:
490	        #     self.world_mesh = init_device_mesh(device_type, (dp_world_size,), mesh_dim_names=(MeshDimName.dp,))
491	        #     return
492	
493	        if dp is None:
494	            raise OLMoConfigurationError(
495	                "Data parallel config is required in addition to expert/tensor/context/pipeline parallel configs"
496	            )
497	
498	        # Validate parallelism degrees while adjusting the dense DP degree. For MoE
499	        # parallel folding, expert parallelism is formed over the folded dense
500	        # DP x CP pool for each PP stage, not over dense DP after CP has divided it.
501	        if pp is not None:
502	            if pp.degree <= 1 or dp_world_size % pp.degree != 0:
503	                raise OLMoConfigurationError(
504	                    f"{pp.__class__.__name__}.degree must be at least 1 and divide into the world size"
505	                )
506	            dp_world_size //= pp.degree
507	        folded_dp_cp_world_size = dp_world_size
508	        if cp is not None:
509	            if cp.degree <= 1 or dp_world_size % cp.degree != 0:
510	                raise OLMoConfigurationError(
511	                    f"{cp.__class__.__name__}.degree must be at least 1 and divide into the world size"
512	                )
513	            dp_world_size //= cp.degree
514	        if tp is not None:
515	            if tp.degree <= 1 or dp_world_size % tp.degree != 0:
516	                raise OLMoConfigurationError(
517	                    f"{tp.__class__.__name__}.degree must be at least 1 and divide into the world size"
518	                )
519	            dp_world_size //= tp.degree
520	        # A negative EP degree is the "use all remaining ranks" shorthand: expert parallelism
521	        # spans the whole folded DP x CP pool.
522	        ep_degree = folded_dp_cp_world_size if ep is not None and ep.degree < 0 else None
523	        if ep is not None:
524	            if ep_degree is None:
525	                ep_degree = ep.degree
526	            if ep_degree <= 1 or folded_dp_cp_world_size % ep_degree != 0:
527	                raise OLMoConfigurationError(
528	                    f"{ep.__class__.__name__}.degree must be at least 1 and divide into the "
529	                    f"folded DP x CP world size, got folded_dp_cp_world_size={folded_dp_cp_world_size} and ep.degree={ep.degree}"
530	                )
531	
532	        # Build up dense mesh dimensions. (PP, DP, CP)
533	        names: List[str] = []
534	        dims: List[int] = []
535	
536	        # Pipeline parallel first.
537	        use_paired_pp = False  # TODO: move to config
538	        # TODO 2: implement paired pp properly
539	        if pp is not None:
540	            names.append(MeshDimName.pp)
541	            if use_paired_pp:
542	                dims.append(pp.degree // 2)
543	            else:
544	                dims.append(pp.degree)
545	
546	        # Then data parallel.
547	        names.append(MeshDimName.dp)
548	        dims.append(dp_world_size)
549	
550	        # Context parallel ranks share data-loader batches with the same DP rank,
551	        # but participate in dense parameter gradient synchronization.
552	        if cp is not None:
553	            names.append(MeshDimName.cp)
554	            dims.append(cp.degree)
555	
556	        if pp is not None and use_paired_pp:
557	            names.append("pp_paired")
558	            dims.append(2)
559	
560	        with torch.device("cpu"):
561	            mesh = torch.arange(math.prod(tuple(dims)), dtype=torch.int).view(tuple(dims))
562	
563	        if pp is not None and use_paired_pp:
564	            r = mesh.permute(0, 2, 1).contiguous()
565	            pp_dim, pp_paired, dp_dim = r.shape
566	            r_merged = r.reshape(pp_dim * pp_paired, dp_dim)  # (pp*pp_paired, dp)
567	            mesh = r_merged
568	            names.remove("pp_paired")
569	
570	        self.dense_mesh = DeviceMesh(
571	            device_type=device_type,
572	            mesh=mesh,
573	            mesh_dim_names=tuple(names),
574	        )
575	        # self.dense_mesh = init_device_mesh(device_type, tuple(dims), mesh_dim_names=tuple(names))
576	        log.info(f"Built dense_mesh {get_device_mesh_info(self.dense_mesh)}")
577	
578	        if ep is None:  # EP not used
579	            self.moe_mesh = None
580	            log.info("Built moe_mesh None")
581	
582	        else:
583	            # Build up moe mesh dimensions using MoE parallel folding. The dense
584	            # DP x CP pool is reinterpreted as EP_DP x EP_MP so CP does not
585	            # multiply the minimum GPU requirement for EP.
586	            names = []
587	
588	            # Pipeline parallel first.
589	            if pp is not None:
590	                names.append(MeshDimName.pp)
591	
592	            assert ep_degree is not None
593	            ep_dp_world_size = folded_dp_cp_world_size // ep_degree
594	            names.append(MeshDimName.ep_dp)
595	            names.append(MeshDimName.ep_mp)
596	
597	            with torch.device("cpu"):
598	                dense_rank_grid = self.dense_mesh.mesh.detach().cpu().to(torch.int)
599	                if pp is not None:
600	                    pp_world_size_for_layout = pp.degree // 2 if use_paired_pp else pp.degree
601	                    folded_rank_grid = dense_rank_grid.reshape(
602	                        pp_world_size_for_layout,
603	                        folded_dp_cp_world_size,
604	                    )
605	                    mesh = folded_rank_grid.reshape(
606	                        pp_world_size_for_layout,
607	                        ep_dp_world_size,
608	                        ep_degree,
609	                    )
610	                else:
611	                    folded_rank_grid = dense_rank_grid.reshape(folded_dp_cp_world_size)
612	                    mesh = folded_rank_grid.reshape(ep_dp_world_size, ep_degree)
613	
614	            device_mesh = DeviceMesh(
615	                device_type=device_type,
616	                mesh=mesh,
617	                mesh_dim_names=tuple(names),
618	            )
619	            self.moe_mesh = device_mesh
620	            # self.moe_mesh = init_device_mesh(device_type, tuple(dims), mesh_dim_names=tuple(names))
621	
622	            log.info(f"Built moe_mesh{get_device_mesh_info(self.moe_mesh)}")
623	
624	        # build process group
625	
626	        if pp is not None:
627	            # self.dense_mesh['pp'] and self.moe_mesh['pp'] should be the same
628	            self.pp_group = self.dense_mesh["pp"].get_group()  #
629	
630	        self.dp_group = self.dense_mesh["dp"].get_group()
631	        if cp is not None:
632	            self.cp_group = self.dense_mesh["cp"].get_group()
633	            self.dense_dp_cp_group, _dense_dp_cp_groups = self._build_mesh_dim_process_group(
634	                self.dense_mesh,
635	                (MeshDimName.dp, MeshDimName.cp),
636	                group_desc="moe_v2_dense_dp_cp",
637	            )
638	        else:
639	            self.cp_group = None
640	            self.dense_dp_cp_group = self.dp_group
641	        if self.moe_mesh is not None:
642	            self.ep_dp_group = self.moe_mesh["ep_dp"].get_group()
643	            self.ep_mp_group = self.moe_mesh["ep_mp"].get_group()
644	            # Under parallel folding, CP is already folded into the MoE EP-DP axis.
645	            self.expert_param_group = self.ep_dp_group
646	
647	        self.world_mesh = {
648	            "dense": self.dense_mesh,
649	            "moe": self.moe_mesh,
650	            "dense_cpu": cpu_mesh_like(self.dense_mesh),
651	            "moe_cpu": None if self.moe_mesh is None else cpu_mesh_like(self.moe_mesh),
652	        }

654	    @staticmethod
655	    def _mesh_dim_rank_groups(device_mesh: DeviceMesh, dims: Sequence[str]) -> List[List[int]]:
656	        if device_mesh.mesh_dim_names is None:
657	            raise RuntimeError("could not build process groups without mesh dimension names")
658	
659	        dim_names = tuple(device_mesh.mesh_dim_names)
660	        target_dims = tuple(str(dim) for dim in dims)
661	        missing_dims = [dim for dim in target_dims if dim not in dim_names]
662	        if missing_dims:
663	            raise RuntimeError(
664	                f"could not build process groups for dimensions {target_dims} from mesh "
665	                f"with dimensions {dim_names}"
666	            )
667	
668	        target_dim_indices = [dim_names.index(dim) for dim in target_dims]
669	        other_dim_indices = [idx for idx in range(len(dim_names)) if idx not in target_dim_indices]
670	
671	        rank_grid = device_mesh.mesh.detach().cpu().to(torch.int64)
672	        permuted = rank_grid.permute(*(other_dim_indices + target_dim_indices)).contiguous()
673	        target_shape = tuple(rank_grid.shape[idx] for idx in target_dim_indices)
674	        target_size = math.prod(target_shape)
675	
676	        if not other_dim_indices:
677	            return [[int(rank) for rank in permuted.reshape(target_size).tolist()]]
678	
679	        rank_groups: List[List[int]] = []
680	        other_shape = tuple(rank_grid.shape[idx] for idx in other_dim_indices)
681	        for index in product(*(range(size) for size in other_shape)):
682	            group = permuted[index].reshape(target_size).tolist()
683	            rank_groups.append([int(rank) for rank in group])
684	        return rank_groups
685	
686	    @classmethod
687	    def _build_mesh_dim_process_group(
688	        cls,
689	        device_mesh: DeviceMesh,
690	        dims: Sequence[str],
691	        *,
692	        group_desc: str,
693	    ) -> Tuple[ProcessGroup, List[ProcessGroup]]:
694	        current_group, all_groups = dist.new_subgroups_by_enumeration(
695	            cls._mesh_dim_rank_groups(device_mesh, dims),
696	            group_desc=group_desc,
697	        )
698	        if current_group == dist.GroupMember.NON_GROUP_MEMBER:
699	            raise RuntimeError(
700	                f"Current rank is not in any process group for mesh dimensions {tuple(dims)}"
701	            )
702	        return cast(ProcessGroup, current_group), cast(List[ProcessGroup], all_groups)

801	    def _estimate_pp_rowwise_lifetime_lease_slots_by_stage(self) -> Dict[int, int]:
802	        if self._train_pp_schedule is None:
803	            return {}
804	        schedule_impl = getattr(self._train_pp_schedule, "schedule_impl", None)
805	        pipeline_order = getattr(schedule_impl, "pipeline_order", None)
806	        rank = getattr(schedule_impl, "rank", None)
807	        if pipeline_order is None or rank is None or rank not in pipeline_order:
808	            return {}
809	
810	        from olmo_core.train.train_module.transformer.pipeline.pipeline_schedule import (
811	            PipelineActionType,
812	        )
813	
814	        active_by_stage: Dict[int, int] = {}
815	        high_water_by_stage: Dict[int, int] = {}
816	        for action in pipeline_order[rank]:
817	            if action is None:
818	                continue
819	            if action.computation_type == PipelineActionType.FORWARD:
820	                stage_active = active_by_stage.get(action.stage_index, 0) + 1
821	                active_by_stage[action.stage_index] = stage_active
822	                high_water_by_stage[action.stage_index] = max(
823	                    high_water_by_stage.get(action.stage_index, 0),
824	                    stage_active,
825	                )
826	            elif action.computation_type == PipelineActionType.FULL_BACKWARD:
827	                active_by_stage[action.stage_index] = max(
828	                    0,
829	                    active_by_stage.get(action.stage_index, 0) - 1,
830	                )
831	        return {stage_idx: max(1, slots) for stage_idx, slots in high_water_by_stage.items()}
832	
833	    def _estimate_pp_rowwise_lifetime_lease_slots_for_model_parts(self) -> List[int]:
834	        if self._pp_stages is None:
835	            return [1 for _ in self.model_parts]
836	
837	        high_water_by_stage = self._estimate_pp_rowwise_lifetime_lease_slots_by_stage()
838	        fallback = max(1, int(getattr(self._train_pp_schedule, "num_microbatches", 1)))
839	        slots_by_part = [
840	            max(1, int(high_water_by_stage.get(stage.stage_index, fallback)))
841	            for stage in self._pp_stages
842	        ]
843	        if len(slots_by_part) != len(self.model_parts):
844	            raise RuntimeError(
845	                "Could not size rowwise lifetime lease slots per PP model part: "
846	                f"got {len(slots_by_part)} stages for {len(self.model_parts)} model parts"
847	            )
848	        log.info(
849	            "Prewarming rowwise lifetime lease slots per local PP stage: %s",
850	            {stage.stage_index: slots for stage, slots in zip(self._pp_stages, slots_by_part)},
851	        )
852	        return slots_by_part

854	    def _pp_dry_run_num_microbatches(self, full_num_microbatches: int) -> int:
855	        raw_value = os.getenv("OLMO_PP_DRY_RUN_MICROBATCHES")
856	        if raw_value is None:
857	            requested = 2 * max(1, self.pp_group_size)
858	        else:
859	            normalized = raw_value.strip().lower()
860	            if normalized in {"", "0", "false", "no", "off", "full"}:
861	                return full_num_microbatches
862	            try:
863	                requested = int(normalized)
864	            except ValueError as exc:
865	                raise OLMoConfigurationError(
866	                    "OLMO_PP_DRY_RUN_MICROBATCHES must be a positive integer, " "'0', or 'full'"
867	                ) from exc
868	            if requested <= 0:
869	                return full_num_microbatches
870	
871	        return max(1, min(full_num_microbatches, requested))

920	    def _maybe_reduce_pp_dry_run_batch(
921	        self,
922	        input_ids: torch.Tensor,
923	        labels: torch.Tensor,
924	        model_kwargs: Dict[str, Any],
925	    ) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, Dict[str, Any], Optional[int]]:
926	        assert self.pp_enabled
927	
928	        full_num_microbatches = self._pp_full_num_microbatches()
929	        dry_run_num_microbatches = self._pp_dry_run_num_microbatches(full_num_microbatches)
930	        if dry_run_num_microbatches >= full_num_microbatches:
931	            return input_ids, labels, model_kwargs, None
932	
933	        original_batch_size = input_ids.size(0)
934	        if original_batch_size % full_num_microbatches != 0:
935	            raise OLMoConfigurationError(
936	                "Cannot reduce PP dry-run microbatches without changing per-microbatch shape: "
937	                f"input batch size {original_batch_size} is not divisible by "
938	                f"full_num_microbatches={full_num_microbatches}"
939	            )
940	
941	        instances_per_microbatch = original_batch_size // full_num_microbatches
942	        dry_run_batch_size = dry_run_num_microbatches * instances_per_microbatch
943	
944	        log.info(
945	            "Reducing PP dry-run from %d to %d microbatches "
946	            "(rank batch %d -> %d, per-microbatch batch size %d)",
947	            full_num_microbatches,
948	            dry_run_num_microbatches,
949	            original_batch_size,
950	            dry_run_batch_size,
951	            instances_per_microbatch,
952	        )
953	
954	        return (
955	            input_ids[:dry_run_batch_size].contiguous(),
956	            labels[:dry_run_batch_size].contiguous(),
957	            {
958	                key: self._slice_pp_batch_dim(value, original_batch_size, dry_run_batch_size)
959	                for key, value in model_kwargs.items()
960	            },
961	            dry_run_num_microbatches,

982	        self,

1150	    def save_state_dict_direct(
1151	        self,
1152	        dir: PathOrStr,
1153	        *,
1154	        process_group: Optional[dist.ProcessGroup] = None,
1155	        save_overwrite: bool = False,
1156	        thread_count: Optional[int] = None,
1157	        process_count: Optional[int] = None,
1158	        throttle_uploads: bool = False,
1159	        compact_storage: bool = False,
1160	        dedup_save_to_lowest_rank: bool = True,
1161	        constant_memory_planning: bool = False,
1162	        profile: bool = False,
1163	    ) -> Optional[Dict[str, float]]:
1164	        """Save native optimizer/model state and restore the live optimizer's storage.
1165	
1166	        Defaults preserve the existing writer policy. ``compact_storage`` skips copies only
1167	        for compact CPU storage; ``process_count`` selects the writer's existing spawn pool.
1168	        ``constant_memory_planning`` computes metadata for ordinary contiguous shards
1169	        arithmetically, with the default planner as fallback for other layouts.
1170	        ``profile`` logs per-rank phases and summed worker time separately from wall time.
1171	        CPU profiling uses wall time; CUDA profiling synchronizes this module's device.
1172	        Profiling returns durations in seconds plus writer byte/item counts; otherwise returns None.
1173	        """
1174	
1175	        def timestamp():
1176	            if profile:
1177	                if self.device.type == "cuda":
1178	                    torch.cuda.synchronize(self.device)
1179	                return time.perf_counter()
1180	            return 0.0
1181	
1182	        start = timestamp()
1183	        timings: Dict[str, float] = {}
1184	        optim = self._require_optimizer()
1185	        # Validate the path and writer options before state_dict releases optimizer storage.
1186	        dir = _prepare_env_for_save(dir, process_group=process_group, save_overwrite=save_overwrite)
1187	        writer = RemoteFileSystemWriter(
1188	            dir,
1189	            thread_count=thread_count,
1190	            process_count=process_count,
1191	            process_group=process_group,
1192	            throttle_uploads=throttle_uploads,
1193	            compact_storage=compact_storage,
1194	            profile=profile,
1195	        )
1196	        planner = FlatSavePlanner(
1197	            dedup_save_to_lowest_rank=dedup_save_to_lowest_rank,
1198	            constant_memory_planning=constant_memory_planning,
1199	            profile=profile,
1200	        )
1201	        if profile:
1202	            timings["prepare_seconds"] = timestamp() - start
1203	        phase_start = timestamp()
1204	        state_dict = optim.state_dict()
1205	        if profile:
1206	            timings["state_dict_seconds"] = timestamp() - phase_start
1207	        try:
1208	            phase_start = timestamp()
1209	            save_dict = dict(state_dict)
1210	            for key, buffer in self._persistent_model_buffer_state_dict().items():
1211	                assert (
1212	                    key not in save_dict
1213	                ), f"Buffer key '{key}' collides with an optimizer state key"
1214	                save_dict[key] = buffer
1215	            if profile:
1216	                timings["buffers_seconds"] = timestamp() - phase_start
1217	            phase_start = timestamp()
1218	            dist_cp.state_dict_saver.save(
1219	                save_dict, storage_writer=writer, process_group=process_group, planner=planner
1220	            )
1221	            if profile:
1222	                timings["distributed_save_seconds"] = timestamp() - phase_start
1223	                timings.update(writer.timings)
1224	                timings.update(planner.timings)
1225	        finally:
1226	            phase_start = timestamp()
1227	            optim.load_state_dict(state_dict, reset_optimizer_moments_on_load=False)
1228	            if profile:
1229	                timings["optimizer_reload_seconds"] = timestamp() - phase_start
1230	            phase_start = timestamp()
1231	            torch.cuda.empty_cache()
1232	            if profile:
1233	                timings["empty_cache_seconds"] = timestamp() - phase_start
1234	                timings["total_seconds"] = timestamp() - start
1235	                log.info("checkpoint_save %s", json.dumps(timings, sort_keys=True))
1236	        return timings if profile else None

1487	    def _get_model_state_dict_for_eval_load(self, metadata: Metadata) -> Dict[str, Any]:
1488	        model_state: Dict[str, Any] = {}
1489	        checkpoint_keys = set(metadata.state_dict_metadata.keys())
1490	
1491	        for model_part in self.model_parts:
1492	            for name, param in model_part.named_parameters():
1493	                checkpoint_key = self._resolve_model_checkpoint_key(name, checkpoint_keys)
1494	                if checkpoint_key is None:
1495	                    continue
1496	
1497	                tensor_meta = metadata.state_dict_metadata[checkpoint_key]
1498	                assert isinstance(tensor_meta, TensorStorageMetadata)
1499	                global_numel = tensor_meta.size.numel()
1500	                is_optimizer_main_param = checkpoint_key.endswith(".main")
1501	                local_tensor = param.data.view(-1) if is_optimizer_main_param else param.data
1502	                local_numel = local_tensor.numel()
1503	                global_shape = (
1504	                    (global_numel,) if is_optimizer_main_param else tuple(tensor_meta.size)
1505	                )
1506	
1507	                if (
1508	                    self.expand_shared_qk_norm_on_load
1509	                    and name.endswith((".q_norm.weight", ".k_norm.weight"))
1510	                    and param.ndim == 2
1511	                    and tuple(tensor_meta.size) == (param.shape[1],)
1512	                ):
1513	                    # Replicated Q/K gains are not EP shards. Keep the live destination;
1514	                    # the load wrapper reads a temporary shared vector and expands it.
1515	                    model_state[checkpoint_key] = local_tensor
1516	                    continue
1517	
1518	                if local_numel == global_numel:
1519	                    model_state[checkpoint_key] = local_tensor
1520	                else:
1521	                    moe_mesh = self.world_mesh["moe"]
1522	                    if moe_mesh is None:
1523	                        raise RuntimeError(
1524	                            f"Cannot load checkpoint tensor '{checkpoint_key}' for parameter "
1525	                            f"'{name}' in eval mode with expert parallelism disabled: checkpoint "
1526	                            f"has {global_numel:,d} elements but the model parameter has "
1527	                            f"{local_numel:,d} elements. EP=1 eval can load EP-trained "
1528	                            f"checkpoints when the checkpoint and model configs match; this "
1529	                            f"shape mismatch usually means the eval config does not match the "
1530	                            f"checkpoint."
1531	                        )
1532	
1533	                    ep_mp_size = moe_mesh["ep_mp"].size()
1534	                    expected_global_numel = local_numel * ep_mp_size
1535	                    if expected_global_numel != global_numel:
1536	                        raise RuntimeError(
1537	                            f"Cannot load checkpoint tensor '{checkpoint_key}' for sharded "
1538	                            f"parameter '{name}' in eval mode: checkpoint has "
1539	                            f"{global_numel:,d} elements, but the local parameter has "
1540	                            f"{local_numel:,d} elements across EP-MP size {ep_mp_size:,d} "
1541	                            f"({expected_global_numel:,d} total). This usually means the "
1542	                            f"eval config does not match the checkpoint."
1543	                        )
1544	
1545	                    model_state[checkpoint_key] = DTensor.from_local(
1546	                        local_tensor,
1547	                        device_mesh=moe_mesh["ep_dp", "ep_mp"],
1548	                        placements=[Replicate(), Shard(0)],
1549	                        shape=global_shape,
1550	                        stride=self._contiguous_stride(global_shape),
1551	                        run_check=False,
1552	                    )
1553	
1554	        if not model_state:
1555	            raise RuntimeError("Did not find any model weights to load in eval mode")
1556	
1557	        return model_state

1559	    @staticmethod
1560	    def _contiguous_stride(shape: Sequence[int]) -> Tuple[int, ...]:
1561	        stride: List[int] = []
1562	        running = 1
1563	        for dim in reversed(shape):
1564	            stride.append(running)
1565	            running *= int(dim)
1566	        return tuple(reversed(stride))

1570	    @staticmethod
1571	    def _strip_wrapper_prefixes(name: str) -> str:
1572	        while True:
1573	            for prefix in ("module.", "_orig_mod."):
1574	                if name.startswith(prefix):
1575	                    name = name[len(prefix) :]
1576	                    break
1577	            else:
1578	                return name

1580	    def _persistent_model_buffer_state_dict(self) -> Dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
1581	        """
1582	        Map each persistent model buffer to a stable checkpoint key.
1583	
1584	        Persistent buffers (e.g. the router's aux-loss-free ``score_bias``) hold learned state that
1585	        is updated outside the optimizer, so they must be checkpointed alongside optimizer state.
1586	        Keys are stripped of DDP / ``torch.compile`` wrapper prefixes so a checkpoint saved from the
1587	        wrapped training model reloads into the unwrapped eval model and vice versa.
1588	        """
1589	        buffer_state: Dict[str, torch.Tensor] = {}
1590	        for model_part in self.model_parts:
1591	            for module_name, module in model_part.named_modules():
1592	                for buffer_name, buffer in module._buffers.items():
1593	                    if buffer is None or buffer_name in module._non_persistent_buffers_set:
1594	                        continue
1595	                    full_name = f"{module_name}.{buffer_name}" if module_name else buffer_name
1596	                    key = self._MODEL_BUFFER_KEY_PREFIX + self._strip_wrapper_prefixes(full_name)
1597	                    if key in buffer_state:
1598	                        raise RuntimeError(
1599	                            f"Duplicate persistent buffer checkpoint key '{key}'; buffer names "
1600	                            "collide across model parts."
1601	                        )
1602	                    buffer_state[key] = buffer
1603	        return buffer_state
1604	
1605	    def _resolve_model_checkpoint_key(
1606	        self, param_name: str, checkpoint_keys: Collection[str]
1607	    ) -> Optional[str]:
1608	        param_names: List[str] = []
1609	        for candidate_name in (param_name, self._strip_wrapper_prefixes(param_name)):
1610	            if candidate_name not in param_names:
1611	                param_names.append(candidate_name)
1612	
1613	        candidates: List[str] = []
1614	        for candidate_name in param_names:
1615	            candidates.extend(
1616	                (
1617	                    f"model.{candidate_name}",
1618	                    f"model.module.{candidate_name}",
1619	                    candidate_name,
1620	                    f"module.{candidate_name}",
1621	                    f"{candidate_name}.main",
1622	                    f"module.{candidate_name}.main",
1623	                )
1624	            )
1625	        for key in candidates:
1626	            if key in checkpoint_keys:
1627	                return key
1628	        return None

def apply_fsdp(
        self,
        dp_mesh: Optional[DeviceMesh] = None,
        param_dtype: Optional[torch.dtype] = None,
        reduce_dtype: torch.dtype = torch.float32,
        pp_enabled: bool = False,
        prefetch_factor: int = 0,
        wrapping_strategy: TransformerDataParallelWrappingStrategy = TransformerDataParallelWrappingStrategy.full,
    ):
        """
        Apply FSDP(2) to the model.

        .. warning::
            This should generally be called last if using any other parallelism strategies or optimizations
            like :meth:`apply_compile()`.

        :param dp_mesh: The model data parallel device mesh.
        :param param_dtype: The data type to materialize params in. Defaults to the current param dtype.
        :param reduce_dtype: The data type for gradient reduction.
        :pp_enabled: If pipeline parallelism is also enabled.
        :prefetch_factor: For tuning the prefetch settings. 0 is the default, and higher values result
            in more aggressive prefetching.
        :wrapping_strategy: The wrapping strategy.
        """
        mp_policy = MixedPrecisionPolicy(
            param_dtype=param_dtype or self.dtype, reduce_dtype=reduce_dtype
        )
        fsdp_config = dict(mesh=dp_mesh, mp_policy=mp_policy)
        # For PP, do not reshard after forward to avoid per-microbatch all-gathers,
        # which can be expensive and non-overlapped
        reshard_after_forward = False if pp_enabled else True

        for block in self.blocks.values():
            block = cast(TransformerBlockBase, block)
            block.apply_fsdp(
                dp_mesh=dp_mesh,
                prefetch_factor=prefetch_factor,
                wrapping_strategy=wrapping_strategy,
                reshard_after_forward=reshard_after_forward,
                mp_policy=mp_policy,
            )

        # When weights are tied the embeddings and LM head share a parameter, so they must
        # stay in the same FSDP group (the root) rather than being sharded separately.
        if self.embeddings is not None and not self.tie_word_embeddings:
            fully_shard(
                self.embeddings,
                reshard_after_forward=reshard_after_forward,
                **fsdp_config,
            )
            # Embedding params are not needed for backwards computation.
            cast(FSDPModule, self.embeddings).set_unshard_in_backward(False)

        if wrapping_strategy != TransformerDataParallelWrappingStrategy.blocks:
            if self.embedding_norm is not None:
                fully_shard(self.embedding_norm, **fsdp_config)
            if self.lm_head is not None and not self.tie_word_embeddings:
                fully_shard(self.lm_head, reshard_after_forward=False, **fsdp_config)

        fully_shard(self, reshard_after_forward=reshard_after_forward, **fsdp_config)
        # Some inputs need to be on CPU initially, but FSDP will move everything to model's
        # device if we don't hide it.
        self.register_forward_pre_hook(_hide_cpu_inputs_from_torch, prepend=True, with_kwargs=True)
        self.register_forward_pre_hook(
            _unhide_cpu_inputs_from_torch, prepend=False, with_kwargs=True
        )

        if prefetch_factor > 0:
            blocks = cast(List[FSDPModule], list(self.blocks.values()))
            for i in range(len(blocks)):
                block = blocks[i]
                if i + 1 < len(blocks):
                    block.set_modules_to_forward_prefetch(blocks[i + 1 : i + 1 + prefetch_factor])
                elif isinstance(self.lm_head, FSDPModule):
                    block.set_modules_to_forward_prefetch([self.lm_head])

        self._fsdp_enabled = True

    def apply_ddp(
        self,
        dp_mesh: Optional[DeviceMesh] = None,
        param_dtype: Optional[torch.dtype] = None,
        compile_enabled: bool = False,
        autograd_compile_enabled: bool = False,
    ):
        """
        Apply DDP to the model.
        """
        from torch.distributed._composable.replicate import replicate

        # Cast model explicitly to the specified dtype before applying DDP
        target_dtype = param_dtype or self.dtype
        if target_dtype != self.dtype:
            self.to(dtype=target_dtype)

        # Adapted from
        # https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/blob/90c889e972b56b9faadebbb78fc985dedc537ed9/torchtitan/parallelisms/parallelize_llama.py#L328
        if compile_enabled:
            if autograd_compile_enabled:
                torch._dynamo.config.optimize_ddp = "python_reducer_without_compiled_forward"  # type: ignore
            else:
                torch._dynamo.config.optimize_ddp = "ddp_optimizer"  # type: ignore

        replicate(self, device_mesh=dp_mesh, bucket_cap_mb=100)
        # Some inputs need to be on CPU initially, but DDP will move everything to model's
        # device if we don't hide it.
        self.register_forward_pre_hook(_hide_cpu_inputs_from_torch, prepend=True, with_kwargs=True)
        self.register_forward_pre_hook(
            _unhide_cpu_inputs_from_torch, prepend=False, with_kwargs=True
        )

    @cached_property
    def num_params(self) -> int:
        return sum(p.numel() for p in self.parameters())

    @property
    def num_trainable_params(self) -> int:
        return sum(p.numel() for p in self.parameters() if p.requires_grad)

    @cached_property
    def num_non_embedding_params(self) -> int:
        return self.num_params - self.embeddings.weight.numel()

    def num_flops_per_token(self, seq_len: int) -> int:
        """
        Returns the idealized number of flops per token for the given sequence length. Purposefully
        does not account for wasted flops due to padding, recomputation, etc.
        """
        flops_per_token = 0
        blocks = cast(List[TransformerBlockBase], list(self.blocks.values()))

import logging
from typing import List, Optional, TypeVar, cast

import torch
from torch.distributed import DeviceMesh

from olmo_core.distributed.parallel import (
    DataParallelType,
    get_cp_mesh,
    get_device_mesh_info,
    get_dp_model_mesh,
    get_ep_mesh,
    get_pp_mesh,
    get_tp_mesh,
)
from olmo_core.exceptions import OLMoConfigurationError
from olmo_core.float8 import Float8Config
from olmo_core.nn.transformer import MoETransformer, Transformer

from .config import (
    TransformerActivationCheckpointingConfig,
    TransformerContextParallelConfig,
    TransformerDataParallelConfig,
    TransformerExpertParallelConfig,
    TransformerTensorParallelConfig,
)

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)


M = TypeVar("M", Transformer, List[Transformer])


def parallelize_model(
    model: M,
    *,
    world_mesh: Optional[DeviceMesh],
    device: torch.device,
    max_sequence_length: Optional[int] = None,
    rank_microbatch_size: Optional[int] = None,
    compile_model: bool = False,
    float8_config: Optional[Float8Config] = None,
    dp_config: Optional[TransformerDataParallelConfig] = None,
    tp_config: Optional[TransformerTensorParallelConfig] = None,
    cp_config: Optional[TransformerContextParallelConfig] = None,
    ep_config: Optional[TransformerExpertParallelConfig] = None,
    ac_config: Optional[TransformerActivationCheckpointingConfig] = None,
    pp_enabled: bool = False,
) -> M:
    model_parts: List[Transformer] = [model] if isinstance(model, Transformer) else model

    pp_mesh: Optional[DeviceMesh] = None
    if pp_enabled:
        assert world_mesh is not None
        pp_mesh = get_pp_mesh(world_mesh)
        for m in model_parts:
            m.apply_pp(pp_mesh)

    # Maybe apply FP8 training.
    if float8_config is not None and float8_config.enabled:
        for m in model_parts:
            m.apply_fp8(float8_config)
            log.info("Swapped linear layers to Float8 linear layers\n%s", m)

    # Maybe apply context parallelism.
    if cp_config is not None:
        assert world_mesh is not None
        cp_mesh = get_cp_mesh(world_mesh)
        for m in model_parts:
            m.apply_cp(cp_mesh, ring=cp_config.ring, uly=cp_config.uly)
        log.info(f"Applied context parallelism to the model with {get_device_mesh_info(cp_mesh)}")

    # Maybe apply tensor.
    if tp_config is not None:
        if ep_config is not None:
            raise NotImplementedError("TP + EP is not implemented yet")
        assert world_mesh is not None
        tp_mesh = get_tp_mesh(world_mesh)
        for m in model_parts:
            m.apply_tp(tp_mesh)
        tp_config.maybe_enable_async_tp(tp_mesh)
        log.info(f"Applied tensor parallelism to the model with {get_device_mesh_info(tp_mesh)}")

    # Maybe apply expert parallelism.
    if ep_config is not None:
        assert world_mesh is not None
        ep_mesh = get_ep_mesh(world_mesh)
        for m in model_parts:
            if not m.is_moe:
                raise OLMoConfigurationError("Expert parallelism is only valid for MoE models")
            cast(MoETransformer, m).apply_ep(ep_mesh)
        log.info(f"Applied expert parallelism to the model with {get_device_mesh_info(ep_mesh)}")

    # Maybe apply activation checkpointing.
    if ac_config is not None:
        for m in model_parts:
            m.apply_activation_checkpointing(
                ac_config.mode,
                block_interval=ac_config.block_interval,
                modules=ac_config.modules,
                activation_memory_budget=ac_config.activation_memory_budget,
                determinism_check=ac_config.determinism_check,
            )
        log.info(f"Applied '{ac_config.mode}' activation checkpointing to the model")

    # Maybe compile.
    if compile_model:
        if torch.cuda.is_available():
            for m in model_parts:
                m.apply_compile()
            log.info("Applied torch.compile() to the model")
        else:
            log.warning("Skipping model compilation since CUDA is not available")

    # Maybe shard/replicate according to data parallel config.
    if dp_config is not None:
        assert world_mesh is not None
        dp_mesh = get_dp_model_mesh(world_mesh)
        param_dtype = dp_config.param_dtype.as_pt() if dp_config.param_dtype is not None else None
        if dp_config.name in (DataParallelType.fsdp, DataParallelType.hsdp):
            for m in model_parts:
                if m.is_moe:
                    cast(MoETransformer, m).prepare_experts_for_fsdp(
                        world_mesh,
                        param_dtype=param_dtype,
                        reduce_dtype=dp_config.reduce_dtype.as_pt(),
                        pp_enabled=pp_enabled,
                    )
                m.apply_fsdp(
                    dp_mesh=dp_mesh,
                    param_dtype=param_dtype,
                    reduce_dtype=dp_config.reduce_dtype.as_pt(),
                    wrapping_strategy=dp_config.wrapping_strategy,
                    pp_enabled=pp_enabled,
                    prefetch_factor=dp_config.prefetch_factor,
                )
            log.info(f"Applied FSDP to the model with {get_device_mesh_info(dp_mesh)}")
        elif dp_config.name == DataParallelType.ddp:
            for m in model_parts:
                if m.is_moe:
                    cast(MoETransformer, m).prepare_experts_for_ddp(world_mesh)
                m.apply_ddp(dp_mesh=dp_mesh, compile_enabled=compile_model, param_dtype=param_dtype)
            log.info(f"Applied DDP to the model with {get_device_mesh_info(dp_mesh)}")
        else:
            raise NotImplementedError(dp_config.name)

    # Materialize and init parameters.
    log.info("Initializing model weights...")
    for model_part_idx, m in enumerate(model_parts):
        m.init_weights(
            max_seq_len=max_sequence_length,
            max_local_microbatch_size=rank_microbatch_size,
            device=device,
            world_mesh=world_mesh,
            model_part_idx=model_part_idx,
        )

    return model

116	def build_world_mesh(
117	    *,
118	    dp: Optional[DataParallelConfig] = None,
119	    tp: Optional[TensorParallelConfig] = None,
120	    cp: Optional[ContextParallelConfig] = None,
121	    pp: Optional[PipelineParallelConfig] = None,
122	    ep: Optional[ExpertParallelConfig] = None,
123	    device_type: Optional[str] = None,
124	) -> DeviceMesh:
125	    """
126	    Build a :class:`~torch.distributed.device_mesh.DeviceMesh` suitable for the given parallel strategies.
127	
128	    .. seealso::
129	        Pass the mesh created by this function to any of the ``get_*_mesh()`` functions in
130	        this module to get the right sub-mesh for a any given parallel strategy.
131	
132	        - :func:`get_dp_model_mesh()` gives you the 1 or 2D sub-mesh suitable for data parallel *model*
133	          wrappers like FSDP(2) or DDP.
134	        - :func:`get_dp_mesh()` gives you the 1D sub-mesh suitable for configuring *data loaders*.
135	        - :func:`get_tp_mesh()` gives you the 1D sub-mesh for tensor parallelism.
136	        - :func:`get_cp_mesh()` gives you the 1D sub-mesh for context parallelism.
137	        - :func:`get_pp_mesh()` gives you the 1D sub-mesh for pipeline parallelism.
138	        - :func:`get_ep_mesh()` gives you the 1D sub-mesh for expert parallelism.
139	
140	    .. important::
141	        A data parallel config is required if any other parallel config is set.
142	
143	    .. important::
144	        Not all parallel strategies are compatible with each other.
145	
146	    :param dp: Data parallel config.
147	    :param tp: Tensor parallel config.
148	    :param cp: Context parallel config.
149	    :param pp: Pipeline parallel config.
150	    :param ep: Expert parallel config.
151	    :param device_type: The device type.
152	
153	    :returns: The world mesh with a shape compatible with the given parallel configs.
154	    """
155	    global _WORLD_MESH
156	
157	    if _WORLD_MESH is not None:
158	        raise RuntimeError("world mesh already exists! You can only call 'build_world_mesh' once!")
159	
160	    device_type = device_type or get_default_device().type
161	    dp_world_size = get_world_size()
162	
163	    if pp is None and tp is None and cp is None and dp is None and ep is None:
164	        return init_device_mesh(device_type, (dp_world_size,), mesh_dim_names=(MeshDimName.dp,))
165	
166	    if dp is None:
167	        raise OLMoConfigurationError(
168	            "Data parallel config is required in addition to expert/tensor/context/pipeline parallel configs"
169	        )
170	
171	    # Validate parallelism degrees while adjust the DP degree.
172	    if pp is not None:
173	        if pp.degree < 1 or dp_world_size % pp.degree != 0:
174	            raise OLMoConfigurationError(
175	                f"{pp.__class__.__name__}.degree must be at least 1 and divide into the world size"
176	            )
177	        dp_world_size //= pp.degree
178	    if cp is not None:
179	        if cp.degree < 1 or dp_world_size % cp.degree != 0:
180	            raise OLMoConfigurationError(
181	                f"{cp.__class__.__name__}.degree must be at least 1 and divide into the world size"
182	            )
183	        dp_world_size //= cp.degree
184	    if tp is not None:
185	        if tp.degree < 1 or dp_world_size % tp.degree != 0:
186	            raise OLMoConfigurationError(
187	                f"{tp.__class__.__name__}.degree must be at least 1 and divide into the world size"
188	            )
189	        dp_world_size //= tp.degree
190	    if ep is not None:
191	        if ep.degree == 0 or dp_world_size % ep.degree != 0:
192	            raise OLMoConfigurationError(
193	                f"{ep.__class__.__name__}.degree must be at least 1 and divide into the world size"
194	            )
195	        if tp is not None:
196	            raise OLMoConfigurationError(
197	                "expert parallelism is mutually exclusive with tensor parallism"
198	            )
199	        # With HSDP we just reuse the 'dp_shard' dimension for expert sharding.
200	        if dp.name != DataParallelType.hsdp:
201	            dp_world_size //= ep.degree
202	
203	            # TODO: remove this restriction once DTensor supports cross-mesh operations.
204	            raise OLMoConfigurationError(
205	                "expert parallelism can currently only be used with HSDP data parallelism"
206	            )
207	
208	    # Build up mesh dimensions.
209	    names: List[str] = []
210	    dims: List[int] = []
211	
212	    # Pipeline parallel first.
213	    if pp is not None:
214	        names.append(MeshDimName.pp)
215	        dims.append(pp.degree)
216	
217	    # Then data parallel.
218	    if dp.name == DataParallelType.hsdp:
219	        num_replicas, shard_degree = dp.get_replicate_and_shard_degree(dp_world_size)
220	        names.append(MeshDimName.dp_replicate)
221	        dims.append(num_replicas)
222	        names.append(MeshDimName.dp_shard)
223	        dims.append(shard_degree)
224	
225	        # Expert parallel.
226	        if ep is not None:
227	            # We just reuse the 'dp_shard' dimension for expert sharding.
228	            if ep.degree >= 0 and ep.degree != shard_degree:
229	                raise OLMoConfigurationError(
230	                    "expert parallelism + HSDP requires the same sharding degree"
231	                )
232	    else:
233	        names.append(MeshDimName.dp)
234	        dims.append(dp_world_size)
235	
236	        # Expert parallel.
237	        if ep is not None:
238	            names.append(MeshDimName.ep)
239	            dims.append(ep.degree)
240	
241	    # Context parallel.
242	    if cp is not None:
243	        names.append(MeshDimName.cp)
244	        dims.append(cp.degree)
245	
246	    # And lastly tensor parallel.
247	    if tp is not None:
248	        names.append(MeshDimName.tp)
249	        dims.append(tp.degree)
250	
251	    mesh = init_device_mesh(device_type, tuple(dims), mesh_dim_names=tuple(names))
252	    log.info(f"Built {get_device_mesh_info(mesh)}")
253	
254	    # Ensure data parallel process group is created here.
255	    get_dp_process_group(mesh)
256	
257	    _WORLD_MESH = mesh
258	
259	    return mesh

313	        raise RuntimeError("could not determine DP model sub-mesh without dimension names")

315	    # Expert parallel dims get flattened into a DP dimension.
316	    if MeshDimName.dp in dim_names and MeshDimName.ep in dim_names:

326	            device_mesh,
327	            MeshDimName.ep_replicate,
328	            MeshDimName.ep_shard,
329	            name=MeshDimName.dp,

334	    # NOTE: We do this because for param-synchronization purposes a CP group behaves like an extra
335	    # DP replica set. CP splits the context across ranks but every CP rank still holds a copy of

337	    if MeshDimName.cp in dim_names:

343	            MeshDimName.cp,

553	    *dims: str,
554	    name: Optional[str] = None,

556	) -> Tuple[DeviceMesh, Tuple[str, ...]]:
